stem.text: A radioactive sample decays by emitting $\beta^{-}$ particles.
The energy released in the decay process is the same for each nucleus that decays, but the $\beta^{-}$ particles emitted have a continuous range of kinetic energies.
Which statement explains why the $\beta^{-}$ particles are emitted with a continuous range of kinetic energies?

A.text: Some of the energy released is given to the remaining nucleons in the nucleus.

B.text: Some of the energy released is taken by an emitted antineutrino.

C.text: Some of the energy released is used to create the $\beta^{-}$ particle.

D.text: Some of the energy released is used to create a new nucleon.
